summary.headline: Orchid Pharma Q4 FY26 standalone revenue flat YoY at ~INR238 crore with EBITDA ~INR42.3 crore; FY26 EBITDA fell to INR101 crore from INR155 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was about INR238 crore, broadly flat versus about INR237 crore in Q4 FY25, and EBITDA rose to about INR42.3 crore from about INR40 crore. Full-year FY26 revenue fell to INR811 crore from INR922 crore and EBITDA fell to INR101 crore from INR155 crore, with management attributing this to cephalosporin price erosion and inventory write-downs in Q1 to Q3. Management said gross margins recovered in Q4 and that the worst of the pricing cycle may be behind, while remaining cautious on a full industry recovery. The call also covered the pending Dhanuka Laboratories merger, the 7ACA project, Enmetazobactam out-licensing (no definitive deal signed yet), and a planned US sterile cephalosporin fill-finish push.

segments.name: Base cephalosporin business
segments.commentary: Management is targeting 10-15% growth for FY27 and about 12% EBITDA margin for the base business. Growth is expected mainly from non-regulated markets such as Africa and South Asia.

segments.name: Enmetazobactam (Exblifep)
segments.commentary: Currently sold only in India and Europe; Europe Q1 sales were about 4x the prior quarter but not yet financially meaningful. Lifetime sales guided at $1-2 billion, with peak now expected in year 4-5 after launch.

segments.name: AMS (antimicrobial stewardship)
segments.commentary: Growing steadily and gaining hospital recognition. Currently an EBITDA drag of about INR8 crore a year.

segments.name: Dhanuka Laboratories (pending merger)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR450 crore, down from INR500 crore; EBITDA not yet available as audit is ongoing. Management estimates the merger could add 1-2% to combined EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: Base business growth target of 10-15% in FY27, with about 12% EBITDA margin assumed for FY27.
7ACA project commissioning targeted for Q1 CY2027 at Chennai; first sales go internally, third-party sales after first few quarters.
Cefiderocol facility to be commissioned by end CY2026; product launch expected in Q2 or Q3 CY2027, subject to approvals.
Shionogi-linked plant commissioning in December 2026; India launch expected about six months after a clinical trial waiver, i.e. second half CY2027.
Enmetazobactam out-licensing: management hopes to sign at least one deal in the current quarter and about 50% of the identified markets within six months.
Merger with Dhanuka Laboratories: court order reserved in March; written order expected after court vacations.
capex_capacity: Cefiderocol facility: 1 million vial capacity; estimated first-few-years demand about 400,000 vials, with about one-third for India and the rest global; cost-plus agreement with guaranteed fixed PBT.
US sterile fill-finish and formulation capex about INR50 crore, mostly within the Cefiderocol project and largely filing and development expense.

7ACA: about 75% of output to be consumed in-house (25% existing consumption plus downstream intermediates); downstream capacity to be added by reengineering existing plants, with budget set aside; management guided about 5% additional EBITDA from downstream products.

US sterile FDF plan: five to six large sterile products over next few years, addressing about two-thirds of a ~$1.2 billion US cephalosporin opportunity; first ANDAs (Ceftazidime-Avibactam and Ceftaroline) to be filed via a CMO, with Orchid site as second site later.
demand_pricing: Cephalosporin pricing rose in April 2026 on war-related input cost increases (solvents and inputs); management reviews prices almost weekly and is unsure how much cost increases can be passed on.
7ACA price about $61/kg, versus about $55 a couple of quarters ago; long-term average about $60, with a range of $55-65.
Q2 and Q3 FY26 saw inventory bought at high prices sold at lower market prices, causing gross margin pressure; management said Q1 FY26 likely had the largest inventory loss but did not quantify it.
Cefiderocol price cited by analyst at about $150 per vial; management did not confirm the figure.
Enmetazobactam in Europe depends on formulary and government tender inclusion; South Europe inclusion is driving sales growth. Enmetazobactam treated about 30,000 patients in the last year.

qa_highlights.question: Why has no Enmetazobactam out-licensing deal been signed despite the earlier one-per-quarter expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Mridul Dhanuka said long-term agreements are taking longer than expected; term sheets are signed in some markets and definitive agreements are under negotiation in Japan, Russia, US, Latin America and Southeast Asia. Management hopes for one deal this quarter and expects about 50% of these to be signed within six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the base business margin and growth outlook for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is targeting about 12% EBITDA margin and 10-15% sales growth in FY27, continuing a four-to-five-year trend. It noted that non-regulated market pricing will stay competitive as capacity expands.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Dhanuka merger a change in 7ACA in-house consumption (75%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Mridul Dhanuka said 25% is existing consumption and the rest will be converted into downstream intermediates sold from Orchid Chennai. Only about 20-25% of 7ACA will be sold to third parties; some downstream capacity addition is needed, reengineering existing plants first.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak sales and timing for Enmetazobactam?
qa_highlights.answer: Lifetime sales are still held at $1-2 billion over the patent life. Peak sales are now expected in the fourth or fifth year after launch rather than the third.

qa_highlights.question: How will Cefiderocol capacity utilisation ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1 million vials is sufficient and no near-term expansion is needed. About 400,000 vials are expected in the first few years, depending on geographies opened through GARDP licensing.

qa_highlights.question: Will US ANDAs be filed from a CMO first?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Ceftazidime-Avibactam and Ceftaroline will be filed through a CMO first to avoid delay from US FDA facility approval, with the Orchid site added later as an alternate manufacturing site.

risks_watch: Pending written order on the Dhanuka Laboratories merger; synergy of 1-2% EBITDA margin depends on completion.
FY26 EBITDA down about 35% YoY; sustainability of Q4 gross margin recovery and price increases amid war-related cost inflation.
Enmetazobactam out-licensing timing: no definitive agreement signed yet; deal flow repeatedly deferred.
7ACA commissioning in Q1 CY2027 described as a race against time; downstream capacity capex still unquantified.
Cefiderocol and US sterile launch timelines depend on regulatory approvals and registrations.
Chinese capacity additions and competitive pricing in non-regulated markets.
summary.management_tone: Confident on strategy and the stabilising pricing backdrop, but cautious on a full industry recovery. Management was evasive on Enmetazobactam deal timing, product-level numbers and the Dhanuka EBITDA, citing confidentiality and audit timing.
key_quotes: While we still remain cautious in calling this a full industry recovery, the business environment currently appears significantly more stable compared to last few quarters.
We now believe the company is entering the next phase, which is platform creation.
So we hope we can continue between 10% to 15% again this year. That's our target.
I would not be able to put a number, but we believe that the first quarter, the loss was the maximum because we were carrying inventory having planned for a good growth during the year.
